claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its FCC ternary and quaternary subsets are governed by variations in local lattice distortion.
The degree and spatial distribution of chemical short-range order modulate local lattice distortions in these alloys.
Local lattice distortions and short-range order alter dislocation mobility and interactions.
Composition-dependent local strain fields arise from differences in atomic-size mismatch and bonding environments.
Local strain fields and short-range order influence twinning activation.
Local strain fields and short-range order influence dynamic strain aging.
Changes in dislocation behavior, twinning, or dynamic strain aging produce differences in yield strength and work-hardening rate.
The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline is single-phase FCC.
The selected ternary and quaternary specimens can be compared as single-phase FCC alloys after similar thermomechanical processing.
Mechanical behavior differs between the quinary alloy and at least some of its equiatomic FCC derivatives.
In situ synchrotron XRD and pair-distribution-function analysis can quantify evolving local lattice-parameter fluctuations and short-range-order metrics during deformation.
Ternary or quaternary alloys with reduced or more uniformly distributed local lattice distortion should have lower yield strength than the quinary baseline.
Reduced or more uniformly distributed local lattice distortion may enhance ductility.
Local-distortion and short-range-order metrics should correlate systematically with yield strength, ductility, or work-hardening behavior.
The proposed relationship is limited to similarly processed, single-phase FCC alloys under ambient-temperature quasi-static loading and is not asserted for dynamic loading or transformation regimes.
